facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
no history of liver disease
leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2)
Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts

concepts.why: The patient developed jaundice, loss of appetite, and malaise after starting Alfuzosin, with significantly elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, suggesting a drug-induced liver injury.
Although the patient's alpha-1 antitrypsin level was normal, the diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out without further testing, and the patient's liver disease could be related to this condition.
The patient's presentation with jaundice, dark urine, and elevated bilirubin levels, in the absence of any obvious cause, could suggest an idiopathic acute cholestasis.
Although the patient's autoimmune markers were negative, the diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis cannot be entirely ruled out, and the patient's liver disease could be related to this condition.

Although the patient's serologic tests for viral hepatitis were negative, the diagnosis of viral hepatitis cannot be entirely ruled out, and the patient's liver disease could be related to this condition.
